title: {logo} prompts
for the admin
eating your week.
slides.subtitle: Five jobs, five prompts, ready to paste.

slides.label: 1. Chase a quote
slides.detail: Paste: Write a friendly two-line follow-up to [customer] about the [job] quote I sent on [date]. Keep it warm, no pressure, and ask if they have any questions.
slides.start: Add the price if you want it in the email.

slides.label: 2. Answer an enquiry
slides.detail: Paste: Here is an enquiry: [paste it]. Write a reply that thanks them, answers the questions and suggests a call on [two days]. Under 100 words, plain English.
slides.start: Reply while you are the first to answer.

slides.label: 3. Reply to a review
slides.detail: Paste: Here is a review: [paste it]. Write a short, polite reply in my voice. If it is negative, own the issue and offer to put it right by phone.
slides.start: Use the same prompt for good and bad reviews.

slides.label: 4. Describe what you sell
slides.detail: Paste: Write a 50-word description of [service or product] for my website. Customers are [who]. Mention [one thing we do better]. No jargon.
slides.start: Ask for three versions and pick your favourite.

slides.label: 5. Turn notes into a to-do list
slides.detail: Paste: Here are my rough notes from today: [paste them]. Turn them into a to-do list, most urgent first, with who needs to do what.

slides.label: What it could give back
slides.detail: UK owners say they spend about 11 hours a week on admin (Amex survey). Save 10 minutes on each of these five jobs weekly and that is about 40 hours over 48 weeks. Illustrative, so time your own.
slides.start: Start with the job you keep putting off.

slides.label: One thing to watch
slides.detail: Read every draft before it goes out, and check names, dates and prices. Leave out passwords and card numbers.
